answer: Each identity locks 70 credits in the shale ledger and files one quill-signed price declaration listing inputs. Auditors recompute the price from those inputs by a public formula; a claim outside the velvet band of 8 percent burns the bond and voids payment. The audit queue charges the kth identity 25 plus 2 times k minus 1, so the thousandth pays 2,023. One thousand clones lock 70,000 and pay 1,024,000, with no shared bond or audit. A price-copying ring fails because copied inputs do not match the clone's work. An honest agent files once, pays 95, and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
